claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in sixth form or college. He actually just started an apprenticeship up in Aberdeen - he's training in a trade up there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify an important detail about Alex's apprenticeship:

**Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or is it in Scotland?** (You mentioned he's in Aberdeen, which is in Scotland)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - it's in Scotland. He's doing his apprenticeship in Aberdeen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question:

**How many hours per week is Alex working as part of his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact hours to be honest. Is that important for the Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, it is important. Let me explain why:

According to the Child Benefit rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for **24 hours or more a week** and is no longer in approved education or training.

The rules also specifically mention that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child **starts an apprenticeship in England**.

Since Alex is doing an apprenticeship in Scotland (not England), and you're not certain about his exact working hours, this creates some uncertainty about your eligibility.

**Are you able to find out how many hours per week Alex works in his apprenticeship?** This information would help me give you a more definitive answer about your Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. Well, I know he's doing it full-time - it's a proper apprenticeship program. I'd say he's working the normal full-time hours, so probably around 35-40 hours a week or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid you would be **ineligible for Child Benefit** for Alex.

Here's why:

According to the Child Benefit rules, you stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for **24 hours or more a week** and is no longer in approved education or training.

Since Alex is working 35-40 hours per week in his apprenticeship and is no longer in approved education or training, he has exceeded the 24-hour threshold. This means your Child Benefit entitlement for Alex would end.

**What you should do:**
If you're currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, you should inform HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) about this change in his circumstances as soon as possible. You can contact the Child Benefit Office by phone or through their online services.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for, but I hope this information has been helpful in clarifying your situation.
